title: Relationship between fluorescein diacetate-stained hyphae and oxygen utilization, glucose utilization and biomass of submerged fungal batch cultures
blurb: Tests whether fungal threads that pick up fluorescein diacetate stain are truly active, and finds the stain tracks growth, oxygen use and sugar use in lab-grown fungi.

title: The effect of chloroform on protozoa and other soil inhabitants
blurb: A short report on how chloroform fumigation affects soil protozoa and other small soil organisms. [from title]

title: Ultraviolet-induced autofluorescence of arbuscular mycorrhizal root infections: An alternative to clearing and staining methods for assessing infections
blurb: Arbuscules, the tiny feeding structures of mycorrhizal fungi inside roots, glow under ultraviolet light, which gives a quicker way to measure root colonization than clearing and staining.

title: Ultraviolet-induced autofluorescence: a new method for detecting and quantifying vesicular-arbuscular mycorrhizal root infections
blurb: Describes using ultraviolet light to spot and measure mycorrhizal fungi inside plant roots without the usual staining work. [from title]

title: Effects of streptomycin, cycloheximide, fungizone, captan, carbofuran, cygon and PCNB on soil microbe populations and nutrient cycling
blurb: Looks at how a set of common antibiotics, fungicides and insecticides change soil microbe numbers and the cycling of nutrients. [from title]

title: Phosphatase activity of Penicillium citrinum submerged batch cultures and its relationship to fungal activity
blurb: Lab study linking the phosphorus-releasing enzyme activity of a common soil fungus to how active that fungus is. [from title]

title: Rhizosphere bacterial population responses to root colonization by a vesicular-arbuscular mycorrhizal fungus
blurb: Looks at how a mycorrhizal fungus on blue grama roots changes the bacteria living around those roots: some bacterial groups dropped while one species increased.

title: Soil fungi: Measurement of hyphal length
blurb: A short method note on how to measure the length of fungal threads in soil. [from title]

title: Soil fungi: Relationships between hyphal activity and staining with fluorescein diacetate
blurb: Checks whether a fluorescent stain can tell active soil fungi apart from inactive ones. [from title]

title: Filter-out grazers (FOG): A filtration experiment for separating protozoan grazers in soil
blurb: Sets out a filtering method that separates protozoa from the rest of the soil community, so their effect can be studied. [from title]

title: Interactions of bacteria, fungi and their nematode grazers: Effects on nutrient cycling and plant growth
blurb: Plants grown with bacteria and the nematodes that eat them grew faster and took up more nitrogen, because the grazing nematodes released nitrogen the plants could use.

title: Responses of microbial components of the rhizosphere to plant management strategies in semiarid rangeland
blurb: Compares the microbes living around roots under different ways of managing plants on dry rangeland. [from title]

title: Review of the effects of twelve selected biocides on target and non-target soil organisms
blurb: Reviews what common pesticides do to the soil life they were never meant to hit, useful for anyone weighing chemical inputs. [from title]

title: Manipulation of bacteria, fungi and protozoa by biocides in lodgepole pine forest soil microcosms: Effects on organism interactions and nitrogen mineralization
blurb: Uses selective biocides in forest soil to show how cutting back bacteria, fungi or protozoa changes how much plant-available nitrogen the soil releases.

title: Trophic interactions and nitrogen cycling in a semiarid grassland soil. Part I. Seasonal dynamics of the natural populations, their interactions and effects on nitrogen cycling
blurb: Follows soil bacteria, fungi, protozoa and nematodes through the seasons in a dry grassland, and how their feeding links drive nitrogen cycling. [from title]

title: Trophic interactions and nitrogen cycling in a semiarid grassland soil. Part II. System responses to removal of different groups of soil microbes or fauna
blurb: Removes selected groups of soil microbes or animals from grassland soil to see how each group affects nitrogen cycling. [from title]

title: Bacterial, fungal and protozoan responses to chloroform fumigation in stored prairie soil
blurb: Measures how bacteria, fungi and protozoa in stored prairie soil respond to chloroform fumigation, a common step in biomass tests. [from title]

title: Inter- and intraspecific feeding selectivity of Folsomia candida (Willem) (Collembola, Isotomidae) on fungi: Method development and ecological consequences
blurb: Develops a way to test which fungi springtails prefer to eat, and what those food choices mean for soil ecology. [from title]

title: The detrital food web in a short grass prairie
blurb: Maps and measures the detrital food web of a short grass prairie: the soil organisms that feed on dead plant material and on each other. [from title]

title: Carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and sulfur cycling in terrestrial ecosystems
blurb: An overview of how carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and sulfur move through land ecosystems. [from title]

title: Early patterns of heterotroph activity in conifer logs
blurb: Early results from a long-term study of rotting conifer logs, showing how bark and ambrosia beetles open channels and carry in the first decomposer community.

title: Interactions between soil animals and ectomycorrhizal fungal mats
blurb: Explores how small soil animals interact with the dense mats that mycorrhizal fungi form under forest trees. [from title]

title: Nitrogen limitation of decomposition and primary production in short grass, mountain meadow and lodgepole pine forest
blurb: Decomposition and plant growth were tested against added or reduced nitrogen in prairie, meadow and pine forest; each leaf litter broke down fastest in its home ecosystem.

title: Report on the selection of several potentially critical terrestrial systems
blurb: A report for the US Environmental Protection Agency on choosing land ecosystems that may be most at risk. [from title]

title: Social and economic concerns with respect to the choice of critical terrestrial ecosystems
blurb: Considers the social and economic questions involved in deciding which land ecosystems to treat as critical. [from title]

title: A general model of biotic interactions
blurb: Sets out a general model of how living organisms interact with each other, prepared for the US Environmental Protection Agency. [from title]

title: Analysis of food-web structure and function in a short grass prairie, a mountain meadow and lodgepole pine forest
blurb: Compares how soil food webs are built and how they function in a prairie, a mountain meadow and a pine forest. [from title]

title: Seasonal and faunal effects on decomposition in semiarid prairie, meadow and lodgepole pine forest
blurb: Looks at how season and soil animals affect the breakdown of plant litter in prairie, meadow and pine forest. [from title]

title: Use of staining and inhibitors to separate fungal and bacterial activity in soil
blurb: Shows how stains and selective inhibitors can be used to tell fungal activity apart from bacterial activity in soil. [from title]

title: A comparison of agar film techniques for estimating fungal biovolumes in litter and soil
blurb: Compares agar film methods for estimating how much fungus is in leaf litter and soil. [from title]

title: Bioresponse of nontarget organisms resulting from the use of chloropicrin to control laminated root rot in a northwest conifer forest
blurb: Reports how soil organisms that were not the target responded when chloropicrin was used against laminated root rot in a conifer forest. [from title]

title: Comparison of direct versus fumigation incubation microbial biomass estimates in ectomycorrhizal mat and non-mat soils
blurb: Compares two ways of estimating microbial biomass in forest soils with and without dense fungal mats. [from title]

title: Interactions among mycorrhizal fungi, rhizosphere organisms, and plants
blurb: Explains how mycorrhizal fungi change root exudates, nutrient uptake and the wider root-zone food web, with knock-on effects on disease, decomposition, soil structure and plant competition.

title: Microbial characteristics of ectomycorrhizal mat communities in Oregon and California
blurb: Describes the microbes found in dense mycorrhizal fungal mats in forest soils of Oregon and California. [from title]

title: Reduction of microbial and faunal groups following application of streptomycin and captan in Georgia no-till agroecosystems
blurb: Tracks which soil microbes and small animals declined after an antibiotic and a fungicide were applied in no-till fields in Georgia. [from title]

title: Decomposition of fallen trees: Effects of initial conditions and heterotroph colonization rates
blurb: Following newly cut conifer logs for two years shows that the insects and decomposers that move in first, plus the log's own chemistry, shape how fallen trees rot.

title: Evaluation of terrestrial indicators for use in ecological assessments at hazardous waste sites
blurb: A US Environmental Protection Agency report weighing which soil and land indicators work best for assessing hazardous waste sites. [from title]

title: The functional significance and regulation of soil biodiversity: An executive summary of the Soil Ecology Society meeting
blurb: Summarises a Soil Ecology Society meeting on why soil biodiversity matters and what regulates it. [from title]

title: The sustainable biosphere initiative: A commentary from the U.S. Soil Ecology Society
blurb: The US Soil Ecology Society's response to the Sustainable Biosphere Initiative, making the case for soil ecology research. [from title]

title: Use of soil foodweb structure and function to assess superfund sites
blurb: Proposes using the structure and function of the soil food web to assess contaminated Superfund sites. [from title]

title: Population responses of target and non-target forest-soil organisms to selected biocides
blurb: Measures how forest soil organisms, both targeted and untargeted, respond to selected pesticides. [from title]

title: Protozoan communities around conifer roots colonized by ectomycorrhizal fungi

title: Soil organisms and forest health
blurb: A magazine piece on how soil organisms support healthy forests. [from title]

title: Soil protozoa
blurb: A methods chapter on how to sample and count protozoa in soil. [from title]

title: Standard Operating Procedure for Total Bacteria
blurb: A standard lab procedure for counting total bacteria in soil, written for a US Environmental Protection Agency program. [from title]

title: Use of sulfamethoxazole-penicillin, oxytetracycline, carbofuran, carbaryl, naphthalene and Temik to remove key organism groups in soil in a corn agroecosystem

title: Assessing interactions between the soil foodweb and a strain of Pseudomonas putida genetically engineered to degrade 2,4-D

title: Biosafety regulation
blurb: A report on how the release of genetically engineered organisms is, and should be, regulated for safety. [from title]

title: Biosafety regulations: A critique of existing documents
blurb: Critiques existing biosafety regulations for genetically engineered organisms and points out their gaps. [from title]

title: Microflora and microfauna on stems and trunks: Diversity, food webs and effects on plants
blurb: A book chapter on the microbes and tiny animals living on plant stems and tree trunks, and how they affect plants. [from title]

title: Standard Operating Procedure for Microbial Population Dynamics
blurb: A standard lab procedure for measuring how soil microbe populations change over time. [from title]

title: Standard Operating Procedure for Nematode Population and Community Structure
blurb: A standard lab procedure for counting soil nematodes and identifying their feeding groups. [from title]

title: Standard Operating Procedure for Protozoan Populations and Community Structure
blurb: A standard lab procedure for counting soil protozoa and describing their community. [from title]

title: Foundations of bio-diversity in managed Douglas-fir forests
blurb: Discusses what underpins biodiversity in managed Douglas-fir forests, with attention to soil life. [from title]

title: Responses of soil foodweb organisms in the first year following clearcutting and application of chloropicrin to control laminated root rot
blurb: Tracks how soil food web organisms responded in the first year after clearcutting and chloropicrin treatment for laminated root rot. [from title]

title: Changes in rhizosphere microflora and microfauna 10 years following Douglas-fir live tree injection with chloropicrin or methylisothiocyanate

title: Chemistry and microbial activity of forest and pasture riparian-zone soils along three Pacific Northwest streams
blurb: Compares soil chemistry and microbial activity next to streams in forest and pasture land in the Pacific Northwest. [from title]

title: Conventional and organic alternatives to methyl bromide on California strawberries: Effect of Brassica residues and spent mushroom compost following successive chemical fumigation
blurb: On a California strawberry field, one round of broccoli residue or mushroom compost did not rebuild the soil food web enough to replace methyl bromide fumigation.

title: Soil foodweb structure and function in forests: A comparison of conifer, deciduous, riparian and managed forests
blurb: Compares soil food webs under conifer, broadleaf, streamside and managed forests. [from title]

title: Soil microbiology
blurb: A textbook chapter introducing soil microbiology. [from title]

title: Ectomycorrhizae establishment on Douglas-fir seedlings following chloropicrin treatment to control laminated-root rot disease: Assessment 4 and 5 years after outplanting
blurb: Checks whether mycorrhizal fungi established on Douglas-fir seedlings four and five years after chloropicrin treatment for root rot. [from title]

title: Foodweb methodology to assess ecological effects of anthropogenic stressors in soil
blurb: Describes how to use the soil food web to judge the ecological damage that human stresses cause to soil. [from title]

title: Soil organisms and their role in healthy turf
blurb: A magazine article for turf managers on how soil organisms keep turf healthy. [from title]

title: Soil view: Anaerobic bacteria and compost tea
blurb: A short column on anaerobic bacteria and what they mean for compost tea quality. [from title]

title: Sustainable agriculture and the ecology of soil
blurb: Links sustainable farming to the ecology of soil life. [from title]

title: Compost tea, Part I & II
blurb: A two-part magazine introduction to compost tea. [from title]

title: Dynamics of soil fungal and bacterial biomass in a temperate climate alley cropping system
blurb: Follows how fungal and bacterial biomass in soil changes over time in an alley cropping system. [from title]

title: Effects of Klebsiella planticola SDF20 on soil biota and wheat growth in sandy soil
blurb: Tests the effects of a genetically engineered bacterium, Klebsiella planticola SDF20, on soil life and wheat growth in sandy soil. [from title]

title: Soil biology and ecology
blurb: A reference chapter introducing soil biology and ecology. [from title]

title: The Compost Tea Handbook 1.1
blurb: A handbook on making and using compost tea. [from title]

title: The mycorrhizal colonization of six wetland plant species at sites differing in land use history
blurb: Compares mycorrhizal colonization in six wetland plants at sites with different land-use histories. [from title]

title: The Soil Biology Primer, Chapters 1-5: The Soil Foodweb; Soil Bacteria; Soil Fungi; Soil Protozoa; Soil Nematodes
blurb: Dr. Ingham's free, plain-language introduction to soil bacteria, fungi, protozoa and nematodes, written for the US Department of Agriculture. [from title]

title: Brewing compost tea
blurb: A gardening magazine guide to brewing compost tea. [from title]

title: The Compost Tea Brewing Manual
blurb: Dr. Ingham's practical guide to making aerobic compost tea, the method taught in the Soil Food Web School courses. [from title]

title: The functional roles of forest soil arthropods: The soil is a lively place
blurb: A conference paper on the many jobs forest soil arthropods do, and why the soil is a lively place. [from title]

title: Micronized compost and microbial life in compost
blurb: A short column on micronized compost and the microbial life found in compost. [from title]

title: Effect of cover crops and tillage system on symphylan (Symphyla: Scutigerella immaculata, Newport) and Pergamasus quisquiliarum Canestrini (Acari: Mesostigmata) populations
blurb: Looks at how cover crops and tillage affect numbers of garden symphylans, a crop pest, and a predatory mite in the soil. [from title]

title: Wildlife and the remediation of contaminated soils: Extending the analysis of ecological risks to habitat restoration
blurb: A handbook chapter on extending ecological risk assessment of contaminated soils to habitat restoration for wildlife. [from title]

title: Effects of compost amended container media on ornamental plant growth
blurb: Compost replacing peat in container mixes grew ornamental plants as well as or better than the standard mix, and the choice of compost ingredients shaped its chemistry.

title: The soil foodweb: Its role in ecosystem health
blurb: A short piece on the soil food web and its role in keeping ecosystems healthy. [from title]

title: The soil foodweb: soil and composts as living ecosystems
blurb: A conference paper presenting soil and compost as living ecosystems built on the soil food web. [from title]

title: Comparison of soil biota between organic and conventional agroecosystems in Oregon, USA
blurb: Compares the soil organisms found on organic and conventional farms in Oregon. [from title]

title: A comparison of soil food webs beneath C3- and C4-dominated grasslands
blurb: Compares the soil food webs under grasslands dominated by two different types of grasses. [from title]

title: Soil life in reconstructed ecosystems: initial soil food web responses after rebuilding a forest soil profile for a climate change experiment
blurb: Follows how the soil food web responded at first after a forest soil profile was rebuilt for a climate change experiment. [from title]

title: Differences in milk characteristics between a cow herd transitioning to organic versus milk from a conventional dairy herd
blurb: Following a dairy herd moving to organic management, the milk's fatty acid profile shifted once the cows settled into an organic diet, compared with a neighbouring conventional herd.

title: Case study: Comparison of milk composition from adjacent organic and conventional farms in the USA
blurb: Milk from an organic grazing dairy had more conjugated linoleic acid and omega-3 fat in the grazing season than milk from a neighbouring confined conventional herd.

title: Study finds fungi, not plant matter, responsible for most carbon sequestration in northern forests
blurb: A news article on research suggesting that fungi, more than plant matter, are responsible for most carbon storage in northern forests. [from title]

title: Carbon sequestration: The climate change solution that virtually all climate activists ignore
blurb: An opinion piece arguing that storing carbon in soil is an overlooked answer to climate change. [from title]

blurb: A news article on researchers proposing ecological, rather than chemical, ways to control plant disease. [from title]

title: Compost could be worth double or triple of current price only if…
blurb: An article on what would need to change for compost to be valued at a higher price. [from title]

title: Predatory earwigs are attracted by herbivore-induced plant volatiles linked with plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria
blurb: Predatory earwigs were drawn most to plants that had both beneficial root bacteria and caterpillar damage, showing how soil microbes can help call in natural pest enemies.

title: The control of diseases on lettuce by the use of antagonistic organisms. 1. The control of Botrytis cinerea Pers.
blurb: An early study showing that selected bacteria, actinomycetes and fungi sprayed onto lettuce could protect leaves and young plants from grey mould rot.

title: Litter decomposition under snow cover in a balsam fir forest
blurb: Measures how fir needles, birch leaves, lichens and twigs keep breaking down under deep winter snow, with decomposers active well before spring melt.

title: Biological nitrogen fixation for sustainable agriculture: A perspective
blurb: Reviews the role biological nitrogen fixation can play in sustainable farming. [from title]

title: Compost and compost water extract-induced systemic acquired resistance in cucumber and Arabidopsis
blurb: A disease-suppressive compost mix, and water extracts made from it, switched on whole-plant defences in cucumber and Arabidopsis, and the effect came from living organisms in the compost.

title: Trophic relationships in the soil microfood-web: Predicting the responses to a changing global environment
blurb: Reviews how predators and food supply regulate the soil food web, and how rising carbon dioxide, land use and plant changes may ripple through soil life.

title: Heavy metals bioremediation of soil
blurb: Reviews ways of using living organisms to clean heavy metals out of soil. [from title]

title: In situ and in vitro suppressive effect of agricultural composts and their water extracts on some phytopathogenic fungi
blurb: Tests how well farm composts and their water extracts hold back several plant disease fungi in the field and in the lab. [from title]

title: Top-down is bottom-up: Does predation in the rhizosphere regulate aboveground dynamics?
blurb: Argues that predators feeding around plant roots release nutrients that drive plant growth, so the whole pattern of root-zone feeding links life below and above ground.

title: Compost tea as a container medium drench for suppressing seedling damping-off caused by Pythium ultimum
blurb: Compares ways of brewing compost tea for preventing damping-off in cucumber seedlings; aerated tea made with kelp and humic acid gave the most consistent protection.

title: Microbial growth under the snow: Implications for nutrient and allelochemical availability in temperate soils
blurb: Discusses how microbes keep growing under snow and what that means for nutrients in temperate soils. [from title]

title: Bioremediation potential of spirulina: toxicity and biosorption studies of lead
blurb: Lab tests show live spirulina, a blue-green alga, can soak up low levels of lead from wastewater very quickly.

title: Uptake of lead by a ciliate, Stylonychia mytilus, isolated from industrial effluents: Potential use in bioremediation of wastewater
blurb: Shows a ciliate protozoan from industrial wastewater can take up lead, pointing to a possible use in cleaning wastewater. [from title]

title: Foliar spraying of vermicompost extracts: effects on fruit quality and indications of late-blight suppression of field-grown tomatoes
blurb: Spraying vermicompost extracts on field tomatoes left yields unchanged, and half as many sprayed plants showed clear signs of late blight infection.

title: In vitro and in vivo evaluation of individually compost fungi for potato fusarium dry rot biocontrol
blurb: Eight heat-tolerant fungi taken from compost extracts held back several Fusarium species in the lab and reduced dry rot on treated potato tubers.

title: Suppression of Phytophthora infestans in potatoes by foliar application of food nutrients and compost tea
blurb: Tests foliar sprays of food nutrients and compost tea against late blight in potatoes. [from title]

title: Aerobic compost tea, compost and a combination of both reduce the severity of common scab (Streptomyces scabiei) on potato tubers
blurb: In a New Brunswick potato field, compost, compost tea and both together cut common scab on tubers, and the tea treatments gave higher yields.

title: Chitin signaling in plants: Insights into the perception of fungal pathogens and rhizobacterial symbionts

title: Effect of bacterial isolates obtained from animal manure compost extracts on the development of Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. radicis-lycopersici
blurb: Several bacteria isolated from manure compost extracts held back a tomato crown and root rot fungus in the lab and reduced the disease on seedlings.

title: In vitro studies on control of soil-borne plant pathogens by earthworm Eudrilus eugeniae exudates
blurb: Lab study testing whether fluids from an earthworm species hold back soil-borne plant disease organisms. [from title]

title: Relative effects of biological amendments and crop rotations on soil microbial communities and soilborne diseases of potato
blurb: Compares biological amendments and crop rotations for their effects on soil microbes and soil-borne potato diseases. [from title]

title: Bio-potential of compost tea from agro-waste to suppress Choanephora cucurbitarum L. the causal pathogen of wet rot of okra
blurb: Tests compost tea made from farm waste against the fungus that causes wet rot of okra. [from title]

title: Control of powdery mildew (Erysiphe polygoni) in tomato by foliar applications of compost tea
blurb: Tests foliar sprays of compost tea for controlling powdery mildew on tomatoes. [from title]

title: Potential application of compost teas of agricultural wastes in the control of the mushroom pathogen Verticillium fungicola
blurb: Looks at compost teas from farm waste as a way to control a fungal disease of cultivated mushrooms. [from title]

title: Vermicompost extracts influence growth, mineral nutrients, phytonutrients and antioxidant activity in pak choi (Brassica rapa cv. Bonsai, Chinensis group) grown under vermicompost and chemical fertiliser
blurb: All the vermicompost teas tested boosted pak choi growth and mineral content, mostly through nitrogen, and aeration or additives made little difference to the result.

title: Biocontrol activity and induction of systemic resistance in pepper by compost water extracts against Phytophthora capsici
blurb: Water extracts from some commercial composts held back Phytophthora on peppers, both by acting on the pathogen and by switching on the plant's own defences.

title: Evidence for nitrogen-fixation in the Salicaceae family
blurb: A short report on evidence that willows and poplars may host nitrogen fixation. [from title]

title: Phytotoxicity analysis of extracts from compost and their ability to inhibit soil-borne pathogenic fungi and reduce root-knot nematodes
blurb: Checks compost extracts for harm to plants and for their ability to hold back soil-borne fungi and root-knot nematodes. [from title]

title: Biochemical properties of compost tea associated with compost quality and effects on pak choi growth
blurb: The quality of the starting compost shaped the nutrients, microbial activity and growth substances in compost tea, and therefore how well pak choi grew.

title: Compost and compost tea: Principles and prospects as substrates and soil-borne disease management strategies in soil-less vegetable production

title: Effects and relationships of compost type, aeration and brewing time on compost tea properties, efficacy against Pythium ultimum, phytotoxicity and potential as a nutrient amendment for seedling production
blurb: Compost type, aeration and brewing time all changed compost tea's microbial and chemical make-up, and teas from both composts tested held back the damping-off fungus Pythium.

title: Humic-like substances from different compost extracts could significantly promote cucumber growth
blurb: Reports that humus-like substances extracted from different composts promoted cucumber growth. [from title]

title: In vitro and in vivo evaluation of microbial-enriched compost tea on the development of powdery mildew on melon
blurb: Tests compost tea enriched with microbes against powdery mildew on melon, in the lab and on plants. [from title]

title: Microbiological community analysis of vermicompost tea and its influence on the growth of vegetables and cereals
blurb: Analyses the microbes in aerated vermicompost teas and tests them on vegetables and cereals; field yields did not change, though taste tests picked up differences.

title: Characters of compost teas from different sources and their suppressive effect on fungal phytopathogens
blurb: Compares compost teas made from different sources and how well each holds back fungal plant diseases. [from title]

title: Influence of the nitrogen form on in vitro organogenesis in Equisetum arvense
blurb: In lab cultures of field horsetail, ammonium nitrogen stopped rhizomes and tubers from forming while nitrate did not, showing that the form of nitrogen matters.

title: Non-growing season soil CO2 efflux and its changes in an alpine meadow ecosystem of the Qilian Mountains, Northwest China
blurb: Measures carbon dioxide released from alpine meadow soil outside the growing season in northwest China. [from title]

title: Comparison of seasonal soil microbial process in snow-covered temperate ecosystems of Northern China

title: Using aerated compost tea in comparison with a chemical pesticide for controlling rose powdery mildew

title: Winter soil CO2 flux from different mid-latitude sites from Middle Taihang Mountain in North China

title: Altered carbon delivery from roots: rapid, sustained inhibition of border cell dispersal in response to compost water extracts

title: Biocontrol activity of endophytic fungus of barley, Microdochium bolleyi, against Gaeumannomyces graminis var. tritici

title: Overview of engineering problems of soil compaction and their effects on growth and yields of crops
